The following user(s) said Thank You: Steigo, Michal238 QUICK REPLY REPLY QUOTE THANK YOU https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/homework-dbr-and-rbd/27-drop-base-rallies-and-rally-base-drops 30/34 7/27/2018 Drop Base Rallies and Rally Base Drops - RTM Community DroHpOBMaEse RalEliDesUCaAnTdIORNally BaFsOeRDUMrops MORE LOGOUT #24 whiteout Offline Master Trader jack of all trades master of none Posts: 320 Thank you received: 544 morning dt ..take your time, we are all busy, we reply when we can, no need to sorry. :) about that trade..read this, is from ifmyante So here's what we look for on the charts: General: HTF. Know where price is coming from and going to, and the PA past and present in all the TFs, from the Monthly down. Specific: At the zones you want to trade, look to Past. study the zone in all TFs, down to M1 ask yourself Where were the decisions made? Clean S/D? Mark these lines. No clean S/D? - compressed zone Did price really shoot away form the zone, or did it cp away? Did the zone itself react at the right place? Look beyond the zone further into the past. See what it reacted to. Was there a better S/D nearby that price wants to visit? This explains many fakeouts. https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/homework-dbr-and-rbd/27-drop-base-rallies-and-rally-base-drops 31/34 7/27/2018 Drop Base Rallies and Rally Base Drops - RTM Community Present. EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT HOME Approach. How is price returning to the zone? Where's the nearest flag in the TF you want to trade? This is your tg1 in this TF. Flags in the LTFs? What does PA tell you? Has price tested the last flag on approach? (good sign) Has price compressed into the zone in this TF or LTFs? (good sign) Is there big news on the way? Has there just been big news? Reaction In LTF, does price react violently to the first decision point? Does it quickly engulf the nearest S/D? (good sign) Does price simply CP away? Maybe it wants to go to the next decision point If the first decision point breaks, watch the signs on approach to the next, and, of course, reaction. Chew this over for now. Apply it to your chart history. Apply it to as many failed setups as successful ones. Millions of them if possible! Capture and file them all. This will help make it instinctive so basically rbd and dbr are just one of the things the you have to watch, is like a puzzle, rbd/dbr is one piece, you need others to make the puzzle. That's why we do homeworks, to master all this things togheter and read the price. keep whit homework The following user(s) said Thank You: doubletop, okami, Steigo, azlan1, Michal238, tomerok, adishal, pedrot, JB888, bestgmx, Hydra, grownupchild, salivan Sometimes the horizon disappear. 32/34 https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/homework-dbr-and-rbd/27-drop-base-rallies-and-rally-base-drops 7/27/2018 Drop Base Rallies and Rally Base Drops - RTM Community QUICK REPLY REPLY QUOTE FORUM MORE LOGOUT HOME EDUCATION THANK YOU Drop Base Rallies and Rally Base Drops #25 doubletop Offline Trader 07788814160 Posts: 17 Thank you received: 22 Thanks whiteout, Really appreciate your post thanks. As for your DBR RBD. Please note that some zones you have marked are RBR/DBD. My idea of this assignment is to locate possible turning points, then see how it reacts when price test these levels. Some levels that were "ignored" had prior signs. I would suggest you to look for DBR/RDB that are the strongest. you can define strong level by 2 criterias: 1. How strong was the away move >> then >> its a strong level why:: We assume that at the decision point of breaking the balance (among sellers and buyers) are left with stacks of un-filled orders. 2. How Long was the Price at the defined level before it unbalanced > The least is better. why:: As more time given for buyers and seller to negotiate, the more deals the close. The least time they have to negotiate, we assume for having more un-filled orders left at the zone. There are more ways to define the quality of a level, you will get to learn these with the other HW assignments. Posts: 89 Thank you received: 551 Hi Mel, Thanks for your comments. I value your feedback on my homework. Your observation is correct. When price forms a cluster above demand it is indication that the level will be breached. When price forms a cluster below supply it is indication that the level will be breached. When this happens it is usually the base in a rally-base- rally or drop-base-drop that breaches the level. Is it probably the best indication as to whether a level will fail. I have not been through all the threads, but I have not seen this pointed out yet (I am sure it is, I just have not seen it). In addition, if demand is breach and you get a base directly under the demand, then the breach of the demand may be a false break and price may reverse and run back up trapping the sellers. If supply is breached and you get a base directly above the supply, then the breach of the supply may be a false break and price may reverse and run back down trapping the buyers. I have not seen that mentioned here yet either, though I am sure it's mentioned somewhere. It does not always happen. When it does, there is usually a reason on the left (like in the case).Best when the break is into clear space. https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/homework-dbr-and-rbd/27-drop-base-rallies-and-rally-base-drops?start=350 7/36 7/27/2018 Drop Base Rallies and Rally Base Drops - Page 15 - RTM Community HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT d Attachments: QUICK REPLY REPLY QUOTE THANK YOU madwt - DBR & RBD homework #355 @mel Offline Master Trader Posts: 487 Thank you received: 1115 https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/homework-dbr-and-rbd/27-drop-base-rallies-and-rally-base-drops?start=350 8/36 7/27/2018 Drop Base Rallies and Rally Base Drops - Page 15 - RTM Community Hi OutaHpiOpsMaEnd MadwEtD, UCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT Ok, so here I was refering to the tests in itself so that you could see what happens when an area gets broken. So for a 3:1 R:R I can only risk 33pips. So I have to get the zone smaller. What if you can get this down to a 15 pip risk with the same 100 pip reward. 6:1 R:R. So getting your zones tightened by going to the smaller time frame can be helpful. I used to trade with 4 charts of each currency pair. Daily, 4h, 1h, 15m, each marked with zones. Some people may be able to do this for me it was an exercise in futility. Could not keep track of it all. Miss high time frame info while looking at the lower. So to fix this, I now trade with two charts for each. #1 Monthly, weekly, Daily #2 4h, 1h, 15m Then zones are laid out. Well I sure got wordy. Forgive me Understanding these zones and how to shrink them to increase your profit margin to me is an important aspect of trading profitably. I get kind of excited about it. Hope this is some help. Attachments: 20/36 https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/homework-dbr-and-rbd/27-drop-base-rallies-and-rally-base-drops?start=350 7/27/2018 Drop Base Rallies and Rally Base Drops - Page 15 - RTM Community HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT QUICK REPLY REPLY QUOTE THANK YOU madwt - DBR & RBD homework #365 outapips Visitor Hi madwt, This is my take on how new demand/supply levels are created. Fresh zone are created from an old zone of the opposing type. By that I mean, what was old demand can become fresh supply when price creates a flip zone. On the chart posted lets assume for the purpose of this example that the left hand side of the chart is a price flip zone which means it was previous supply. When price broke thru at (1) it cleared out all the supply so only demand was left at that level. We don't know how strong this is (although how price went thru the level and how far it travelled gives us a clue). There was an initial retest of this level a few bars later which showed there was still plenty of demand. Price came back again at (2) and this is now considered old demand but it was still good enough to hold price again. At point (3) there was a little reaction up consuming the remaining buy orders and so 21/36 https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/homework-dbr-and-rbd/27-drop-base-rallies-and-rally-base-drops?start=350 7/27/2018 Drop Base Rallies and Rally Base Drops - Page 15 - RTM Community demand was all used up and price fell thru creating a new supply zone at that level. HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT Price moved well below the level quite strongly so we can determine this is a good level to short next time back. Point (4) is the first time back to the new supply level so a good place to short. That level is now considered to be old supply. We don't know if a level will hold or how many times a level will hold so we look to the chart for clues. Hope this explanation is clear enough to follow. The thing that drew my eye in was the rally, which lead to the daily close above the area I've marked with a blue line. I've not been able to mark the new level in because it would make the chart quite congested but you'll notice that there is 1 x day of basing and then a day where price drops. I've marked this price drop day as Day 1. To my eyes, the around area around here is a RBD (in the lower timeframes you should also see a DBD) short-term supply level with the nearest area of D1 demand located around the lower wide red line. With the close above and local supply and demand levels in close proximity we must at least now consider the idea that big money has started the process of accumulation. https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/homework-dbr-and-rbd/27-drop-base-rallies-and-rally-base-drops?start=400 12/38 7/27/2018 Drop Base Rallies and Rally Base Drops - Page 17 - RTM Community The day after the drop, i.e. "second day", price pins the area I've marked with a short HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT red line. What caused this pin to occur? The only thing that can cause this pinning above to occur is aggressive selling further confirming our assessment that supply exceeded demand at this "level". You'll see on the candle (again I've not marked it in order to try and keep the chart clean) immediately to the right of "second day" pin bar that price gapped up into the level and then sold off again back down to the close of the second day pinbar. What causes this to happen and why? Once again it is selling. Why is selling occuring here? In order for big money to move the market up it has to buy. Who does it buy from? Sellers. When price moves away from a level, it doesnt matter how soon a re-test back into that comes, thats the highest probability trade because of the probability of unfilled orders resting there. 2. When price rallies back into a previous RBD, the supply that came from the D of that previous RBD was cause of a new area of supply to form that is slightly lower than the previous (often). This causes the lower market structure highs to form, because new levels of supply just below the previous market structure highs has formed, capping price from reaching higher levels. This works both ways, and is what seems to happen many times, not always. 3. Price seems clearer to me that it is always moving around to find piles of orders, and depending on the strength of moves away from those piles, we can reason better about what the probabilities are when price revisits and retests. 4. Wicks or tails mean at the point price reached that extent, there were S/D pushing price faster than the opposing direction, but then that move is overwhelmed by the orders that get touched and filled. https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/homework-dbr-and-rbd/27-drop-base-rallies-and-rally-base-drops?start=450 21/44 7/27/2018 Drop Base Rallies and Rally Base Drops - Page 19 - RTM Community HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT 5. When resting orders sit at these levels, they only execute when market orders take them out, or other execution mechanics force those orders to move to market orders. It is still liquidity takers that must drive price through these levels. 6. When price breaks out of a recent high or base, it often returns on the other side and re-tests. Re-testing suggests a conscious act for price to go test a previous level. To me it seems like it is more a result of price bouncing away from supply and working its way back to value, but as it hits the demand that was strong enough to break those highs, thats were orders exist to give this level support. This is S/R in action. I am sure theres much much more I have missed. But here is my next analysis. Maybe not to the same degree that mettafort and I have just done - we had a common interest but different perspectives to explore, hopefully to the benefit of everyone. A long while back I was in a webinar and the speaker made an almost throw-away statement - which I'm sure sailed straight through most people, but which piqued my interest. It was in response to a question I don't recall, but the reply was, "Although we look at the same charts, we see different things". There was more to it than that, but pondering that statement allowed me to form many questions I didn't even know I needed to ask, then answer them to find more questions. It started me on a path of discoveries - still ongoing - that I doubt I would've walked otherwise. I won't expand beyond that, but what is interesting is that three people looked at roughly the same GBPUSD information and applied their logic to it: two of those people had entirely different opinions of the same RBD and one person ignored it altogether on their chart! So, the benefit comes from the qualitative exercise: 1. What attracted you to this particular RBD or DBR?, what didn't you like? Was your opinion that it would work or not? (Your opinion, mind, not the benefit of 20:20 hindsight ) 2. What happened when price did return to the Base in each case? If it reacted, where (zoom in to the Base and root around)? If it didn't, is there anything that you can learn about it so you can spot a bad-un in the future (that's why we need to find good and bad examples)? https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/homework-dbr-and-rbd/27-drop-base-rallies-and-rally-base-drops?start=450 31/44 7/27/2018 Drop Base Rallies and Rally Base Drops - Page 19 - RTM Community 3. What happened later when price returned to the Base from the other side? Did HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT it react or ignore it again? 4. Zoom out and look back in time, does that change your perception of your chosen examples or help understand why some worked or failed? By going through this process on your charts you will better train your brain to spot and sort these patterns out, and assess the likely turning point within them so you can successfully reduce your exposure in the market (by this I'm sort of referring to R:R, but I'm also taking time into account). And if you keep hitting a wall in your understanding it will better help everyone else to offer suggestions or guidance. You don't need to slap everything on the chart, just your main line of reasoning and points of interest, maybe a little bit of filler in the post, but in doing so you will accelerate your understanding. On the H4 diagram there is a key drop in price which forms a base after a strong move down. This decision point becomes one to continue the down move, and then this area itself becomes a nice supply level. So the base DP provides an area of S or R depending on the move. Bases seem to form a key areas in history where either a S or D level has been known to be present. And even when a supply level at a basing is broken, subsequently when price falls back under again, it can continue to have the same supply pressure as it did once before. A tail/wick into S/D for the first time, seems to suggest a high chance of a second attempt working next time - this chart has lots of double tests before price moves up or down. I am aware of over-analyzing, but I get insights that take my understanding deeper every time I do this. They HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT occur on different time-frames: 1. A2 is on the H4 (first image, lower chart). I draw a tail on the side nearest price so I can check the Price Action history at this level on longer time-frames. The obvious thought is that the more time price spends away from a level, and the greater distance it travels, the more out of balance it is and the more likely that price will react on its return (effectively mean-reversion). I also check reactions to the level, particularly which side price was on just before the zone I'm investigating - I much prefer it to be on the opposite side, indicating that I am looking at a fresh zone (a flip). As I mentioned before I don't like obvious lines of S or R or trend, they are the chart equivalent of the luminescent beacon hanging in front of the Anglerfish's mouth. Here, the last reaction was on the same side, not so attractive 2. A4 is on the H1 chart (second image, upper chart). I check to see how convincingly price moves away from the zone I'm interested in. I like to see long and strong candles with little overlap, and I like to see local opposition levels being taken out easily, preferably to a higher low or a lower high - it shows intent. Here price moves away strongly enough, breaks a small Demand level but turns back at an area that I would consider weak. Again, not so attractive 3. A5 is on the M5 chart (second image, lower chart). As price is leaving the zone for the first time, it spikes it deeply before carrying on. On the retrace, price has to penetrate deeper to find fresh Demand - it does, but that spike was a definite downer So, in weighing up the pros and cons of my observations, this combination was enough to tip the balance against the zone for me. Regards. Spongy. PS. I put together this complex graphic to offer greater insight into the relationship between obvious Support or Resistance levels, or trend lines, and potential pitfalls. The idea is - by repetition - to get your brain to recognise attributes of each so you can hone your skills to spot their viability in real time, and choose prospective turning points within. I do this by asking a series of questions to get me to really look at them, and I refine my questions and observations with each pass. I'm not saying my way is the right way or that I even ask the right questions, just that they cause me to take a good look, and think. Hopefully a pattern database is being built somewhere in the dark recesses of my mind as a result. I wouldn't go so far as to say every peak or trough is RBD or DBR (that's my point of view and I might be entirely wrong, but a spike doesn't necessarily have a base on a shorter time-frame): they can certainly be caps on price, analysis would determine whether they are Supply, Demand or reaction. QUICK REPLY REPLY QUOTE THANK YOU Drop Base Rallies and Rally Base Drops #544 benhur Offline Master Trader www.the5ers.com Posts: 730 Thank you received: 2231 25/35 https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/homework-dbr-and-rbd/27-drop-base-rallies-and-rally-base-drops?start=525 7/27/2018 Drop Base Rallies and Rally Base Drops - Page 22 - RTM Community HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT nichess Nothing promises that zone will hold price, even at first visit. The zones we mark on the charts are mainly a mapping of decisions in the market. Decision can take price either way. Zones are meant to be broken, and this market decision has its own significance too. As further you go with your reading skills, you will be able read the hints and clues for zones to hold or to break. Your task at this time, is to train your eyes defining the zones. Your next step, is to investigate how price is behaving around these zones. there are few things you should bare in mind while you do this work: 1. Be aware of how price had printed the zone you marked, what it was reacting to, and how the decision of price to move further look like. 2. Be aware of how price is approaching the Zones, what is the dynamic. 3. Is price come from a valid opposite zone ? Remember that price goes from Demand to Supply and vice versa. 4. Be aware of the reaction of the first touch, how deep it went inside, what had stopped it if any? 5. what are higher or lower TF tell you. SD discipline is a Multi time frame concept. We trade price levels, not candles, so Story may vary on different TF 6. (more Advanced) Look for correlations with Index and other pairs. it might look intimidating, but actually it's should be very simple. Zones are always a reaction of past Price Action (aka: always look left). As much as you can go back in history, the better your understand be of how price move. there is no randomness for this market, all can be explained with PA reaction, result, decision. just look for reasoning for levels and zones creation. Posts: 463 Thank you received: 910 7a: RBD This is interesting, as it shows why moving your stop to BE is a bad idea, and can take you out of a winning trade, especially if you go short at 7b, the retest of the DP to break the highs of the RBD (this will be a flag on a LTF). The drop from the high of 7a made a decent engulf, so a target at least back down to that engulf, around 'x' would be reasonable. That's only about a 1:1 RRR, though. What I'm learning is that now the DP has been tested, we should watch for shorting opportunities higher into the zone. This setup is also suggesting to me that the retest of the DP (which is 7b) is only likely to be a decent FTR if price has dropped through some strong levels before it returns up to the FTR (I know this is a central teaching of RTM, but this is me now seeing why for myself). If it does not do this, and makes a move back up towards the FTR/meat of the zone, then we should expect price to engulf the FTR upwards, and then turn deeper into the zone. This is another reason the stop should remain above the xone and not be moved to BE until something major is engulfed to the downside. Also, to the left I have marked some 'kind of' compression. There is some fresh demand in there which 7a and 7b have to fight through, but once price moves up to 7c, it's a clearer path down. https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/homework-dbr-and-rbd/27-drop-base-rallies-and-rally-base-drops?start=625 11/29 7/27/2018 Drop Base Rallies and Rally Base Drops - Page 26 - RTM Community HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT Note the compression leading up to 7b and the LQ/FO sucking in the breakout traders to go long. A consolidation below a level suggests that the level will be broken, so it's important to be able to differentiate CP from simple flat price oscillation (that's what a base is, I guess) and a sinking bull flag or you may be going short at a developing RBR, not an imminent drop. So, we want to see HHs and HLs as we approach a supply zone, if price looks like it's ranging below the zone. The Blue line at 7a shows the extreme high of the reaction at 7c. When price gets up to 7c, it has already tested the H1 DP to move down at 7a, so we should "expect" it to now move deeper into the zone, and as it has made some nice engulfs downwards, and been away for some time, we can "expect" to now have a more substantial reaction. But where? Well, the extreme high seems to go to the edge of a CP PAZ at 7a (but I haven't focussed on those, yet) but easier to spot is the QM it has made at 7c. Tyoon : What defines a base is that price moves up or down, bases (consolidates, congests, clusters, etc.) then moves again either up or down. Here are the variations. The standard DBD and RBR then the RBR and DBD then RBD during downtrend and DBR during uptrend. Hopefully this could give you a better understanding. However as you have alluded to, H/L or S/R levels are almost always an intrinsic part to the development of any base. If you can find the levels responsible for the bases it can give you a much holistic picture on the chart. https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/homework-dbr-and-rbd/27-drop-base-rallies-and-rally-base-drops?start=700 16/50 7/27/2018 Drop Base Rallies and Rally Base Drops - Page 29 - RTM Community HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT IF : The two charts on the right, in HTF, can often look just like the two charts on the left. How strong was the away move >> then >> it's a strong level. https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/homework-dbr-and-rbd/27-drop-base-rallies-and-rally-base-drops?start=700 19/50 7/27/2018 Drop Base Rallies and Rally Base Drops - Page 29 - RTM Community Why: We assume that at the decision point of breaking the balance (among sellers and HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT buyers) are left with stacks of un-filled orders. 2. How Long was the Price at the defined level before it unbalanced > the least is better. Why: As more time given for buyers and seller to negotiate, the more deals the close. The least amount of time they have to negotiate, we assume the more un-filled orders left at the zone. IF : One thing which I have mentioned many times before, but not yet in Markepedia (soon to be remedied), is that in a bigger picture range, Supply and Demand zones near the edges may not hold as well as others. Fakeout often occur, because price is attracted to the limits of the range. Benhur : Nothing promises that zone will hold price, even at first visit. The zones we mark on the charts are mainly a mapping of decisions in the market. Decision can take price either way. Zones are meant to be broken, and this market decision has its own significance too. As further you go with your reading skills, you will be able read the hints and clues for zones to hold or to break. Your task at this time, is to train your eyes defining the zones.Your next step, is to investigate how price is behaving around these zones. There are few things you should bare in mind while you do this work: 1. Be aware of how price had printed the zone you marked, what it was reacting to, and how the decision of price to move further look like. 2. Be aware of how price is approaching the Zones, what is the dynamic. 3. Is price come from a valid opposite zone? Remember that price goes from Demand to Supply and vice versa. 4. Be aware of the reaction of the first touch, how deep it went inside, what had stopped it if any? 5. What are higher or lower TF tell you. SD discipline is a Multi time frame concept. We trade price levels, not candles, so Story may vary on different TF. https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/homework-dbr-and-rbd/27-drop-base-rallies-and-rally-base-drops?start=700 20/50 7/27/2018 Drop Base Rallies and Rally Base Drops - Page 29 - RTM Community HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT 6. (More Advanced) Look for correlations with Index and other pairs. It might look intimidating, but actually it's should be very simple. Zones are always a reaction of past Price Action (aka: always look left). As much as you can go back in history, the better you understand be of how price move. There is no randomness for this market, all can be explained with PA reaction, result, decision. Just look for reasoning for levels and zones creation. H1/M15? Thanks CAT Hi CAT, Looking back at my reply to your post, I realise that I did not answer the second part of your question, which was... If this is a strong buy area, which TF do u suggest i look for PA to buy? H1/M15? Unfortunately, there is no black & white (right or wrong) answer to this question. It depends on your trading experience, your trading time frames and personal style. I would answer it by suggesting this... Your should go down time frames until you can clearly identify the decision point that you are expecting to trade a reaction from. If you can see this on a 1 hr chart, than that is suitable. If you can see this on a 15 min chart, than that is suitable. However, the lower the time frame you can pinpoint a decision on, the lower your risk level. In saying that though, lower time frames generally require more time and higher skills. https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/homework-dbr-and-rbd/27-drop-base-rallies-and-rally-base-drops?start=700 36/50 7/27/2018 Drop Base Rallies and Rally Base Drops - Page 29 - RTM Community HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT There are many great RTM traders that trade from 4 hr and 1 hr candles, for example. But, you also have traders like IF that can identify decision points and hence entries on the 1 min chart. I recall a post where a RTM Master was saying that if they cannot identify a clear decision point on the 1 min chart, they will not enter. Just go down to the time frame that allows you to clearly define your entry and risk. If you zoom down and cannot find this, consider skipping the trade. Instead, see where it reacted and then go down to the lower time frames and try to understand why price reacted where it did. It's better than taking a trade your are not 100% sure about, and you will speed up your learning doing this. That's about the best answer I can give. As far was what PA to look for, you can try and use Candle PA but to be honest, reading Candle PA can be quite difficult to interpret correctly. IF goes as far to say that he does not care about candles and gives time no importance at all. Rather, IF looks for decisions on price. IF also says that the best advice he can give you is not to read anything into candles themselves. The two important things to look at for clues as to what price wants to do is Compression and an Engulf. Of the two, the Engulf is the easiest to see and allows the safest trades. Your chart shows a good example on your supply level. Let's take a look. Below is your chart of Gold. To understand why I drew a different supply zone, please see this post by benhur . Posts: 89 Thank you received: 551 gxp1 wrote: hi, In presenting the work on RBD &RBD, i have cheated by using zigzag by first scrolling down the chart.The only reason being that its easy to see major turns. ..... Hi gxp1, Your homework looks good though I would encourage you not to use the zigzag indicator for the following reasons. 1. It will train your eyes faster and better not using the indicator. Instead, focus on the raw price. It may initially be a little more challenging but you will gain much more from your homework exercises. 2. You will miss the more important and subtle RBDs and DBRs on your chart as the indicator will go straight past them. Some of the more important RBDs and DBRs are small subtle ones as opposed to the obvious ones that catches everyone's eye. This post by IF is in this thread is a gem! (I have placed IF's image below.) The small DBR IF points out towards the bottom of the chart (blue box - the `giant omission') would not be picked up via the indicator and is an important DBR. It's also an example of how price reading requires us to piece all the individual parts of price action together. https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/homework-dbr-and-rbd/27-drop-base-rallies-and-rally-base-drops?start=825 14/36 7/27/2018 Drop Base Rallies and Rally Base Drops - Page 34 - RTM Community HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT Why is that small DBR important? What is the minor DBR/RBD? How do we distinguish this from a "normal" zone? Hi DrummerBoy I'll try give an explanation based on how I see things. On any chart we have many DBR's and RBD's, some are large and can extend over time, and in these we often find smaller ones. The following chart demonstrates what I mean. See over time how price has ranged up, based out and then dropped down forming a large RBD https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/homework-dbr-and-rbd/27-drop-base-rallies-and-rally-base-drops?start=850 30/34 7/27/2018 Drop Base Rallies and Rally Base Drops - Page 35 - RTM Community HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT But within that large RBD we can see another smaller RBD, and if we went to a LTF we would find more. So often within a chart we see a combination of smaller RBD/DBR which when combined form a larger one. I'm not sure if this is what was referred to as "minor" / "major" as asked in your question. In the third chart I have just added some other RBD and DBR that I see in the chart for reference. Harry makes a great point here and it's very important to grasp. I have seen many charts marked on the HTF with a FL and then the engulf is shown. Sometimes it looks like the engulf does not work as price continues to charge on. Its worth your time looking at every FL on the LTF and asking yourself where the true limit of the FL is and hence what price level needs to be breached to constitute an engulf. As we are basing our understanding of what price is doing on the engulf of a price level, this is something worth pondering. Here is an example. We expect that the inner boundary of the zone to be the price where remaining stacks of orders are waiting for execution. Since all we have is the chart, we can spot it by a closer look at the candles. There we look where was the last trade before one side overcome the other. Thinking in Order flow terminology, we may suspect that if one side overcome the other, there might be more orders of the winner side which couldent be filled due to less orders of the loosing side. IF : One thing which I have mentioned many times before, but not yet in Markepedia (soon to be remedied), is that in a bigger picture range, Supply and Demand zones near the edges may not hold as well as others. Fakeout often occur, because price is attracted to the limits of the range. Benhur : Nothing promises that zone will hold price, even at rst visit. The zones we mark on the charts are mainly a mapping of decisions in the market. Decision can take price either way. Zones are meant to be broken, and this market decision has its own signi cance too. As further you go with your reading skills, you will be able read the hints and clues for zones to hold or to break. Your task at this time, is to train your eyes de ning the zones.Your next step, is to investigate how price is behaving around these zones. There are few things you should bare in mind while you do this work: 1. Be aware of how price had printed the zone you marked, what it was reacting to, and how the decision of price to move further look like. 2. Be aware of how price is approaching the Zones, what is the dynamic. 3. Is price come from a valid opposite zone? Remember that price goes from Demand to Supply and vice versa. https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/homework-dbr-and-rbd/27-drop-base-rallies-and-rally-base-drops?start=1000 35/42 7/27/2018 Drop Base Rallies and Rally Base Drops - Page 41 - RTM Community 4. Be aware of the reaction of the rst touch, how deep it went inside, what had HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT stopped it if any? 5. What are higher or lower TF tell you. SD discipline is a Multi time frame concept. We trade price levels, not candles, so Story may vary on di erent TF. 6. (More Advanced) Look for correlations with Index and other pairs. It might look intimidating, but actually it's should be very simple. Zones are always a reaction of past Price Action (aka: always look left). As much as you can go back in history, the better you understand be of how price move. There is no randomness for this market, all can be explained with PA reaction, result, decision. When you're doing the DBR/RBD homework, keep that in mind and drag your zones to the right to see how price interacts with them in the future. That will really reinforce the Supply to Demand/Demand to Supply concept and will help when looking at others like FL, FTR, and QM. Posts: 218 Thank you received: 253 Hey Mohsin, Here's what I see on the chart. I have noted a little RBD and DBR within the down trend. I would consider these of lesser importance but if you extend them to the right you can see price reacting off of them as well. I've included them to show you that sometimes we get a longer base in our DBR/RBD. The two of note currently are the top and bottom ones limiting the current flag. I would put the base as the bottom of the candle on this one (the giant pin bar) as the next bar breaks away from it. That pin candle indicates a movement up then down which can also conceal a flag in the LTFs. On this TF I would consider it the base for simplicity's sake. You can get crazy with drawing every blip on the chart and end up with something that will confuse the hell out of you :). Page 49 - RTM Community HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT My homework with explanations at each point A) First DBR B) First RBD (There is a reaction that brings price back to the first demand zone, price flags after touching demand creating a small demand zone on top) Prices reaction to this demand zone cuts through supply at B and this becomes demand C) RBD with a FTB bringing price back to the flag made on top of demand zone at A D) Price reacts to this demand moves away before a FTB pinbar - price easily cuts through supply at C E) RBD - followed by compression down to flip zone from supply at C - from here there is a strong bull move in price that easily breaks supply at E and this becomes demand F) Price is capped and following the indecision there is a RBD formed G) FTB to the strong level created after compression from E H) Price moves up to H where its the FTB to new FTR (plays within this PAZ) I) Bulls are now in control and price is easily able to move down to the price cap at the bottom with a small speed bump from demand at D G) New supply formed where there was previously supply to the left Thanks in advance for all the help! https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/homework-dbr-and-rbd/27-drop-base-rallies-and-rally-base-drops?start=1200 16/34 7/27/2018 Drop Base Rallies and Rally Base Drops - A: Don't get too hung up on the candle count. Focus more on how the price moved away from the level. You want to see a violent burst of liquidity (pole) coming out of the level. What defines a base it that price moves up or down, bases (consolidates, congests, clusters, ect) then moves again either up or down. https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/homework-dbr-and-rbd/27-drop-base-rallies-and-rally-base-drops?start=100 9/34 7/27/2018 Drop Base Rallies and Rally Base Drops - Page 5 - RTM Community Here are the variations. The standard DBD and RBR then the RBR and DBD then RBD HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT during downtrend and DBR during uptrend. Hopefully this could give you a better understanding. However as you have alluded to, H/L or S/R levels are almost always an intrinsic part to the development of any base. If you can find the levels responsible for the bases it can give you a much holistic picture on the chart. Page 50 - RTM Community Thank you received: 56 HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT pin bar is more like this Characteristics of the Pin Bar Formation � The pin bar should have a long upper or lower tail...the tail is also sometimes called the "wick" or the "shadow"...they all mean the same thing. It's the "pointy" part of the pin bar that literally looks like a "tail" and that shows rejection or false break of a level. � The area between the open and close of the pin bar is called the "body" or "real body". It is typically colored white or another light color when the close was higher than the open and black or another dark color when the close was lower than the open. � The open and close of the pin bar should be very close together or equal (same price), the closer the better. � The open and close of the pin bar are near one end of the bar, the closer to the end the better. � The shadow or tail of the pin bar sticks out (protrudes) from the surrounding 22/31 https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/homework-dbr-and-rbd/27-drop-base-rallies-and-rally-base-drops?start=1225 7/27/2018 Drop Base Rallies and Rally Base Drops - Page 50 - RTM Community price bars, the longer the tail of the pin bar the better. We really don't trade those levels directly because this is what classic supply and demand traders do and as we know plain SD trading is just gambling with an (small) edge (IF). The purpose of this homework is to get a feel for basic market structure and to train your eye... And watch out for some tricks too (what happens on ignored levels on return and what happens on stacked levels). Price moves from supply to demand and vice versa. Once you study flag limits you will understand the relationship betweenthe RBD/DBR and FL concept ps. to your question, it makes sense to mark all RBDs and DBRs strong or weak as long as the basic structure is present. First of all, this is a wonderful experience for me to be with you here and learn all this awesome stuff. Next is my HW about caps on price. I used random charts and random segments of them - different TFs. It is really important for me (and my trading) to be as consistent as possible, so here are my rules how I marked rectangles. According to my understanding (mostly coming from the IFs video about the caps) I marked the most important ones, which I identified by liquidity gaps in them. First edge is of course high/low of the cap, but the second edge is open of the last green candle before drop in RBDs and open of the last red candle before the rally in DBR - that is according to my observations the most precise place, where the decision was made to turn the price (IMHO). (If there is no prior candle of different color befor price goes away i marked whole candle in base of the move). note: it really depends on how the rectangle is placed. Sometimes price bounce from the very edges of the base, sometimes from the edge of liquidity gap, but mostly, when I don't want rectangles to be too big, rule above can be applied. note2 : red rectangles don't have reaction if I consider both edges of the rectangle. Price react to them though, but not precisely. note3 : it is obvious that RBD/DBR that are reactions to previous caps are much less important to future visits of price (and it was confirmed by IF and others all over the place ), however price tends to bounce from them too. note4 : because I really like statistics, here are the results from 87 reactions to caps - just for fun, of course: 67 was ok for scalp at least, 4 was fine to trade after they break and 16 was bad. Know where price is coming from and going to, and the PA past and present in all the TFs, from the Monthly down. Specific: At the zones you want to trade, look to Past. study the zone in all TFs, down to M1 ask yourself Where were the decisions made? Clean S/D? Mark these lines. No clean S/D? - compressed zone Did price really shoot away form the zone, or did it cp away? Did the zone itself react at the right place? Look beyond the zone further into the past. See what it reacted to. Was there a better S/D nearby that price wants to visit? This explains many fakeouts. https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/homework-dbr-and-rbd/27-drop-base-rallies-and-rally-base-drops 31/34 7/27/2018 Drop Base Rallies and Rally Base Drops - RTM Community Present. EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT HOME Approach. How is price returning to the zone? Where's the nearest flag in the TF you want to trade? This is your tg1 in this TF. Flags in the LTFs? What does PA tell you? Has price tested the last flag on approach? (good sign) Has price compressed into the zone in this TF or LTFs? (good sign) Is there big news on the way? Has there just been big news? Reaction In LTF, does price react violently to the first decision point? Does it quickly engulf the nearest S/D? (good sign) Does price simply CP away? Maybe it wants to go to the next decision point If the first decision point breaks, watch the signs on approach to the next, and, of course, reaction. Chew this over for now. Apply it to your chart history. Apply it to as many failed setups as successful ones. Millions of them if possible! Capture and file them all. This will help make it instinctive so basically rbd and dbr are just one of the things the you have to watch, is like a puzzle, rbd/dbr is one piece, you need others to make the puzzle. That's why we do homeworks, to master all this things togheter and read the price. keep whit homework The following user(s) said Thank You: doubletop, okami, Steigo, azlan1, Michal238, tomerok, adishal, pedrot, JB888, bestgmx, Hydra, grownupchild, salivan Sometimes the horizon disappear. 32/34 https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/homework-dbr-and-rbd/27-drop-base-rallies-and-rally-base-drops 7/27/2018 Drop Base Rallies and Rally Base Drops - RTM Community QUICK REPLY REPLY QUOTE FORUM MORE LOGOUT HOME EDUCATION THANK YOU Drop Base Rallies and Rally Base Drops #25 doubletop Offline Trader 07788814160 Posts: 17 Thank you received: 22 Thanks whiteout, Really appreciate your post thanks. As you can see on the 1H charts, price has reached a 1H demand level within daily demand. Now this 1H demand zone is fresh and it was reached after price generated a 1H supply zone just above the demand zone. A quick thanks to Redknight for coming up with a great format for marking the charts, helps you keep count of the zones and how succesful they are. https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/homework-dbr-and-rbd/27-drop-base-rallies-and-rally-base-drops?start=325 5/42 7/27/2018 Drop Base Rallies and Rally Base Drops - Page 14 - RTM Community HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT Here are my learning from doing the homework, 1 - scroll slowly through the charts, so that the new candle come up slowly and you can "paper trade". Identify your zones without seeing the reaction, this is key to helping you understand the zones and how they work, and that zones seem to fail at first. 2. read through other peoples homework and get an understanding. In school this was called copying, in this business it's called "benchmarking" and highly encouraged. 3. After a while you will close your eyes and see charts! Here is how to read my notes on my charts. U = untested on this screen R = reaction (normally first) B/E = breakeven, i.e. price reacts, but then goes through the level (decision point) often time you may be able to move your theoritical stop loss to breakeven Ig = ignored (at first) Attachments: https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/homework-dbr-and-rbd/27-drop-base-rallies-and-rally-base-drops?start=325 6/42 7/27/2018 Drop Base Rallies and Rally Base Drops - Posts: 89 Thank you received: 551 Hi Mel, Thanks for your comments. I value your feedback on my homework. Your observation is correct. When price forms a cluster above demand it is indication that the level will be breached. When price forms a cluster below supply it is indication that the level will be breached. When this happens it is usually the base in a rally-base- rally or drop-base-drop that breaches the level. Is it probably the best indication as to whether a level will fail. I have not been through all the threads, but I have not seen this pointed out yet (I am sure it is, I just have not seen it). In addition, if demand is breach and you get a base directly under the demand, then the breach of the demand may be a false break and price may reverse and run back up trapping the sellers. If supply is breached and you get a base directly above the supply, then the breach of the supply may be a false break and price may reverse and run back down trapping the buyers. I have not seen that mentioned here yet either, though I am sure it's mentioned somewhere. It does not always happen. When it does, there is usually a reason on the left (like in the case).Best when the break is into clear space. https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/homework-dbr-and-rbd/27-drop-base-rallies-and-rally-base-drops?start=350 7/36 7/27/2018 Drop Base Rallies and Rally Base Drops - Page 15 - RTM Community HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT d Attachments: QUICK REPLY REPLY QUOTE THANK YOU madwt - DBR & RBD homework #355 @mel Offline Master Trader Posts: 487 Thank you received: 1115 https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/homework-dbr-and-rbd/27-drop-base-rallies-and-rally-base-drops?start=350 8/36 7/27/2018 Drop Base Rallies and Rally Base Drops - Page 15 - RTM Community Hi OutaHpiOpsMaEnd MadwEtD, UCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT Ok, so here I was refering to the tests in itself so that you could see what happens when an area gets broken. Attachments: 20/36 https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/homework-dbr-and-rbd/27-drop-base-rallies-and-rally-base-drops?start=350 7/27/2018 Drop Base Rallies and Rally Base Drops - Page 15 - RTM Community HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT QUICK REPLY REPLY QUOTE THANK YOU madwt - DBR & RBD homework #365 outapips Visitor Hi madwt, This is my take on how new demand/supply levels are created. Fresh zone are created from an old zone of the opposing type. By that I mean, what was old demand can become fresh supply when price creates a flip zone. On the chart posted lets assume for the purpose of this example that the left hand side of the chart is a price flip zone which means it was previous supply. When price broke thru at (1) it cleared out all the supply so only demand was left at that level. We don't know how strong this is (although how price went thru the level and how far it travelled gives us a clue). There was an initial retest of this level a few bars later which showed there was still plenty of demand. Price came back again at (2) and this is now considered old demand but it was still good enough to hold price again. At point (3) there was a little reaction up consuming the remaining buy orders and so 21/36 https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/homework-dbr-and-rbd/27-drop-base-rallies-and-rally-base-drops?start=350 7/27/2018 Drop Base Rallies and Rally Base Drops - Page 15 - RTM Community demand was all used up and price fell thru creating a new supply zone at that level. HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT Price moved well below the level quite strongly so we can determine this is a good level to short next time back. Point (4) is the first time back to the new supply level so a good place to short. That level is now considered to be old supply. We don't know if a level will hold or how many times a level will hold so we look to the chart for clues. Hope this explanation is clear enough to follow. What caused this pin to occur? The only thing that can cause this pinning above to occur is aggressive selling further confirming our assessment that supply exceeded demand at this "level". You'll see on the candle (again I've not marked it in order to try and keep the chart clean) immediately to the right of "second day" pin bar that price gapped up into the level and then sold off again back down to the close of the second day pinbar. What causes this to happen and why? Once again it is selling. Why is selling occuring here? In order for big money to move the market up it has to buy. Who does it buy from? Sellers. Where do sellers and selling occur? At supply levels. What do supply levels look like? When price moves away from a level, it doesnt matter how soon a re-test back into that comes, thats the highest probability trade because of the probability of unfilled orders resting there. 2. When price rallies back into a previous RBD, the supply that came from the D of that previous RBD was cause of a new area of supply to form that is slightly lower than the previous (often). This causes the lower market structure highs to form, because new levels of supply just below the previous market structure highs has formed, capping price from reaching higher levels. This works both ways, and is what seems to happen many times, not always. 3. Price seems clearer to me that it is always moving around to find piles of orders, and depending on the strength of moves away from those piles, we can reason better about what the probabilities are when price revisits and retests. 4. Wicks or tails mean at the point price reached that extent, there were S/D pushing price faster than the opposing direction, but then that move is overwhelmed by the orders that get touched and filled. https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/homework-dbr-and-rbd/27-drop-base-rallies-and-rally-base-drops?start=450 21/44 7/27/2018 Drop Base Rallies and Rally Base Drops - Page 19 - RTM Community HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT 5. When resting orders sit at these levels, they only execute when market orders take them out, or other execution mechanics force those orders to move to market orders. It is still liquidity takers that must drive price through these levels. 6. When price breaks out of a recent high or base, it often returns on the other side and re-tests. Re-testing suggests a conscious act for price to go test a previous level. To me it seems like it is more a result of price bouncing away from supply and working its way back to value, but as it hits the demand that was strong enough to break those highs, thats were orders exist to give this level support. This is S/R in action. I am sure theres much much more I have missed. But here is my next analysis. Maybe not to the same degree that mettafort and I have just done - we had a common interest but different perspectives to explore, hopefully to the benefit of everyone. A long while back I was in a webinar and the speaker made an almost throw-away statement - which I'm sure sailed straight through most people, but which piqued my interest. It was in response to a question I don't recall, but the reply was, "Although we look at the same charts, we see different things". There was more to it than that, but pondering that statement allowed me to form many questions I didn't even know I needed to ask, then answer them to find more questions. It started me on a path of discoveries - still ongoing - that I doubt I would've walked otherwise. I won't expand beyond that, but what is interesting is that three people looked at roughly the same GBPUSD information and applied their logic to it: two of those people had entirely different opinions of the same RBD and one person ignored it altogether on their chart! So, the benefit comes from the qualitative exercise: 1. What attracted you to this particular RBD or DBR?, what didn't you like? Was your opinion that it would work or not? (Your opinion, mind, not the benefit of 20:20 hindsight ) 2. What happened when price did return to the Base in each case? If it reacted, where (zoom in to the Base and root around)? If it didn't, is there anything that you can learn about it so you can spot a bad-un in the future (that's why we need to find good and bad examples)? https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/homework-dbr-and-rbd/27-drop-base-rallies-and-rally-base-drops?start=450 31/44 7/27/2018 Drop Base Rallies and Rally Base Drops - Page 19 - RTM Community 3. What happened later when price returned to the Base from the other side? Did HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT it react or ignore it again? 4. Zoom out and look back in time, does that change your perception of your chosen examples or help understand why some worked or failed? By going through this process on your charts you will better train your brain to spot and sort these patterns out, and assess the likely turning point within them so you can successfully reduce your exposure in the market (by this I'm sort of referring to R:R, but I'm also taking time into account). And if you keep hitting a wall in your understanding it will better help everyone else to offer suggestions or guidance. You don't need to slap everything on the chart, just your main line of reasoning and points of interest, maybe a little bit of filler in the post, but in doing so you will accelerate your understanding. On the H4 diagram there is a key drop in price which forms a base after a strong move down. This decision point becomes one to continue the down move, and then this area itself becomes a nice supply level. So the base DP provides an area of S or R depending on the move. Bases seem to form a key areas in history where either a S or D level has been known to be present. And even when a supply level at a basing is broken, subsequently when price falls back under again, it can continue to have the same supply pressure as it did once before. A tail/wick into S/D for the first time, seems to suggest a high chance of a second attempt working next time - this chart has lots of double tests before price moves up or down. I am aware of over-analyzing, but I get insights that take my understanding deeper every time I do this. They HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT occur on different time-frames: 1. A2 is on the H4 (first image, lower chart). I draw a tail on the side nearest price so I can check the Price Action history at this level on longer time-frames. The obvious thought is that the more time price spends away from a level, and the greater distance it travels, the more out of balance it is and the more likely that price will react on its return (effectively mean-reversion). I also check reactions to the level, particularly which side price was on just before the zone I'm investigating - I much prefer it to be on the opposite side, indicating that I am looking at a fresh zone (a flip). As I mentioned before I don't like obvious lines of S or R or trend, they are the chart equivalent of the luminescent beacon hanging in front of the Anglerfish's mouth. Here, the last reaction was on the same side, not so attractive 2. A4 is on the H1 chart (second image, upper chart). I check to see how convincingly price moves away from the zone I'm interested in. I like to see long and strong candles with little overlap, and I like to see local opposition levels being taken out easily, preferably to a higher low or a lower high - it shows intent. Here price moves away strongly enough, breaks a small Demand level but turns back at an area that I would consider weak. Again, not so attractive 3. A5 is on the M5 chart (second image, lower chart). As price is leaving the zone for the first time, it spikes it deeply before carrying on. On the retrace, price has to penetrate deeper to find fresh Demand - it does, but that spike was a definite downer So, in weighing up the pros and cons of my observations, this combination was enough to tip the balance against the zone for me. Regards. Spongy. PS. I put together this complex graphic to offer greater insight into the relationship between obvious Support or Resistance levels, or trend lines, and potential pitfalls. The idea is - by repetition - to get your brain to recognise attributes of each so you can hone your skills to spot their viability in real time, and choose prospective turning points within. I do this by asking a series of questions to get me to really look at them, and I refine my questions and observations with each pass. I'm not saying my way is the right way or that I even ask the right questions, just that they cause me to take a good look, and think. Hopefully a pattern database is being built somewhere in the dark recesses of my mind as a result. I wouldn't go so far as to say every peak or trough is RBD or DBR (that's my point of view and I might be entirely wrong, but a spike doesn't necessarily have a base on a shorter time-frame): they can certainly be caps on price, analysis would determine whether they are Supply, Demand or reaction. QUICK REPLY REPLY QUOTE THANK YOU Drop Base Rallies and Rally Base Drops #544 benhur Offline Master Trader www.the5ers.com Posts: 730 Thank you received: 2231 25/35 https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/homework-dbr-and-rbd/27-drop-base-rallies-and-rally-base-drops?start=525 7/27/2018 Drop Base Rallies and Rally Base Drops - Page 22 - RTM Community HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT nichess Nothing promises that zone will hold price, even at first visit. The zones we mark on the charts are mainly a mapping of decisions in the market. Decision can take price either way. Zones are meant to be broken, and this market decision has its own significance too. As further you go with your reading skills, you will be able read the hints and clues for zones to hold or to break. Your task at this time, is to train your eyes defining the zones. Your next step, is to investigate how price is behaving around these zones. there are few things you should bare in mind while you do this work: 1. Be aware of how price had printed the zone you marked, what it was reacting to, and how the decision of price to move further look like. 2. Be aware of how price is approaching the Zones, what is the dynamic. 3. Is price come from a valid opposite zone ? Remember that price goes from Demand to Supply and vice versa. 4. Be aware of the reaction of the first touch, how deep it went inside, what had stopped it if any? 5. what are higher or lower TF tell you. SD discipline is a Multi time frame concept. We trade price levels, not candles, so Story may vary on different TF 6. (more Advanced) Look for correlations with Index and other pairs. it might look intimidating, but actually it's should be very simple. Zones are always a reaction of past Price Action (aka: always look left). As much as you can go back in history, the better your understand be of how price move. there is no randomness for this market, all can be explained with PA reaction, result, decision. just look for reasoning for levels and zones creation. Posts: 463 Thank you received: 910 7a: RBD This is interesting, as it shows why moving your stop to BE is a bad idea, and can take you out of a winning trade, especially if you go short at 7b, the retest of the DP to break the highs of the RBD (this will be a flag on a LTF). The drop from the high of 7a made a decent engulf, so a target at least back down to that engulf, around 'x' would be reasonable. That's only about a 1:1 RRR, though. What I'm learning is that now the DP has been tested, we should watch for shorting opportunities higher into the zone. This setup is also suggesting to me that the retest of the DP (which is 7b) is only likely to be a decent FTR if price has dropped through some strong levels before it returns up to the FTR (I know this is a central teaching of RTM, but this is me now seeing why for myself). If it does not do this, and makes a move back up towards the FTR/meat of the zone, then we should expect price to engulf the FTR upwards, and then turn deeper into the zone. This is another reason the stop should remain above the xone and not be moved to BE until something major is engulfed to the downside. Also, to the left I have marked some 'kind of' compression. There is some fresh demand in there which 7a and 7b have to fight through, but once price moves up to 7c, it's a clearer path down. https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/homework-dbr-and-rbd/27-drop-base-rallies-and-rally-base-drops?start=625 11/29 7/27/2018 Drop Base Rallies and Rally Base Drops - Page 26 - RTM Community HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT Note the compression leading up to 7b and the LQ/FO sucking in the breakout traders to go long. A consolidation below a level suggests that the level will be broken, so it's important to be able to differentiate CP from simple flat price oscillation (that's what a base is, I guess) and a sinking bull flag or you may be going short at a developing RBR, not an imminent drop. So, we want to see HHs and HLs as we approach a supply zone, if price looks like it's ranging below the zone. The Blue line at 7a shows the extreme high of the reaction at 7c. When price gets up to 7c, it has already tested the H1 DP to move down at 7a, so we should "expect" it to now move deeper into the zone, and as it has made some nice engulfs downwards, and been away for some time, we can "expect" to now have a more substantial reaction. But where? Well, the extreme high seems to go to the edge of a CP PAZ at 7a (but I haven't focussed on those, yet) but easier to spot is the QM it has made at 7c. Tyoon : What defines a base is that price moves up or down, bases (consolidates, congests, clusters, etc.) then moves again either up or down. Here are the variations. The standard DBD and RBR then the RBR and DBD then RBD during downtrend and DBR during uptrend. Hopefully this could give you a better understanding. However as you have alluded to, H/L or S/R levels are almost always an intrinsic part to the development of any base. If you can find the levels responsible for the bases it can give you a much holistic picture on the chart. https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/homework-dbr-and-rbd/27-drop-base-rallies-and-rally-base-drops?start=700 16/50 7/27/2018 Drop Base Rallies and Rally Base Drops - Page 29 - RTM Community HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT IF : The two charts on the right, in HTF, can often look just like the two charts on the left. How strong was the away move >> then >> it's a strong level. https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/homework-dbr-and-rbd/27-drop-base-rallies-and-rally-base-drops?start=700 19/50 7/27/2018 Drop Base Rallies and Rally Base Drops - Page 29 - RTM Community Why: We assume that at the decision point of breaking the balance (among sellers and HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT buyers) are left with stacks of un-filled orders. 2. How Long was the Price at the defined level before it unbalanced > the least is better. Why: As more time given for buyers and seller to negotiate, the more deals the close. The least amount of time they have to negotiate, we assume the more un-filled orders left at the zone. IF : One thing which I have mentioned many times before, but not yet in Markepedia (soon to be remedied), is that in a bigger picture range, Supply and Demand zones near the edges may not hold as well as others. Fakeout often occur, because price is attracted to the limits of the range. Benhur : Nothing promises that zone will hold price, even at first visit. The zones we mark on the charts are mainly a mapping of decisions in the market. Decision can take price either way. Zones are meant to be broken, and this market decision has its own significance too. As further you go with your reading skills, you will be able read the hints and clues for zones to hold or to break. Your task at this time, is to train your eyes defining the zones.Your next step, is to investigate how price is behaving around these zones. There are few things you should bare in mind while you do this work: 1. Be aware of how price had printed the zone you marked, what it was reacting to, and how the decision of price to move further look like. 2. Be aware of how price is approaching the Zones, what is the dynamic. 3. Is price come from a valid opposite zone? Remember that price goes from Demand to Supply and vice versa. 4. Be aware of the reaction of the first touch, how deep it went inside, what had stopped it if any? 5. What are higher or lower TF tell you. SD discipline is a Multi time frame concept. We trade price levels, not candles, so Story may vary on different TF. https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/homework-dbr-and-rbd/27-drop-base-rallies-and-rally-base-drops?start=700 20/50 7/27/2018 Drop Base Rallies and Rally Base Drops - Page 29 - RTM Community HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT 6. (More Advanced) Look for correlations with Index and other pairs. It might look intimidating, but actually it's should be very simple. Zones are always a reaction of past Price Action (aka: always look left). As much as you can go back in history, the better you understand be of how price move. There is no randomness for this market, all can be explained with PA reaction, result, decision. Just look for reasoning for levels and zones creation. H1/M15? Thanks CAT Hi CAT, Looking back at my reply to your post, I realise that I did not answer the second part of your question, which was... If this is a strong buy area, which TF do u suggest i look for PA to buy? H1/M15? Unfortunately, there is no black & white (right or wrong) answer to this question. It depends on your trading experience, your trading time frames and personal style. I would answer it by suggesting this... Your should go down time frames until you can clearly identify the decision point that you are expecting to trade a reaction from. If you can see this on a 1 hr chart, than that is suitable. If you can see this on a 15 min chart, than that is suitable. However, the lower the time frame you can pinpoint a decision on, the lower your risk level. In saying that though, lower time frames generally require more time and higher skills. https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/homework-dbr-and-rbd/27-drop-base-rallies-and-rally-base-drops?start=700 36/50 7/27/2018 Drop Base Rallies and Rally Base Drops - Page 29 - RTM Community HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT There are many great RTM traders that trade from 4 hr and 1 hr candles, for example. But, you also have traders like IF that can identify decision points and hence entries on the 1 min chart. I recall a post where a RTM Master was saying that if they cannot identify a clear decision point on the 1 min chart, they will not enter. Just go down to the time frame that allows you to clearly define your entry and risk. If you zoom down and cannot find this, consider skipping the trade. Instead, see where it reacted and then go down to the lower time frames and try to understand why price reacted where it did. It's better than taking a trade your are not 100% sure about, and you will speed up your learning doing this. That's about the best answer I can give. As far was what PA to look for, you can try and use Candle PA but to be honest, reading Candle PA can be quite difficult to interpret correctly. IF goes as far to say that he does not care about candles and gives time no importance at all. Rather, IF looks for decisions on price. IF also says that the best advice he can give you is not to read anything into candles themselves. The two important things to look at for clues as to what price wants to do is Compression and an Engulf. Of the two, the Engulf is the easiest to see and allows the safest trades. Your chart shows a good example on your supply level. Let's take a look. Below is your chart of Gold. To understand why I drew a different supply zone, please see this post by benhur . Posts: 89 Thank you received: 551 gxp1 wrote: hi, In presenting the work on RBD &RBD, i have cheated by using zigzag by first scrolling down the chart.The only reason being that its easy to see major turns. ..... Hi gxp1, Your homework looks good though I would encourage you not to use the zigzag indicator for the following reasons. 1. It will train your eyes faster and better not using the indicator. Instead, focus on the raw price. It may initially be a little more challenging but you will gain much more from your homework exercises. 2. You will miss the more important and subtle RBDs and DBRs on your chart as the indicator will go straight past them. Some of the more important RBDs and DBRs are small subtle ones as opposed to the obvious ones that catches everyone's eye. This post by IF is in this thread is a gem! (I have placed IF's image below.) The small DBR IF points out towards the bottom of the chart (blue box - the `giant omission') would not be picked up via the indicator and is an important DBR. It's also an example of how price reading requires us to piece all the individual parts of price action together. https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/homework-dbr-and-rbd/27-drop-base-rallies-and-rally-base-drops?start=825 14/36 7/27/2018 Drop Base Rallies and Rally Base Drops - Page 34 - RTM Community HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT Why is that small DBR important? What is the minor DBR/RBD? How do we distinguish this from a "normal" zone? Hi DrummerBoy I'll try give an explanation based on how I see things. On any chart we have many DBR's and RBD's, some are large and can extend over time, and in these we often find smaller ones. The following chart demonstrates what I mean. See over time how price has ranged up, based out and then dropped down forming a large RBD https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/homework-dbr-and-rbd/27-drop-base-rallies-and-rally-base-drops?start=850 30/34 7/27/2018 Drop Base Rallies and Rally Base Drops - Page 35 - RTM Community HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT But within that large RBD we can see another smaller RBD, and if we went to a LTF we would find more. So often within a chart we see a combination of smaller RBD/DBR which when combined form a larger one. I'm not sure if this is what was referred to as "minor" / "major" as asked in your question. In the third chart I have just added some other RBD and DBR that I see in the chart for reference. Harry makes a great point here and it's very important to grasp. I have seen many charts marked on the HTF with a FL and then the engulf is shown. Sometimes it looks like the engulf does not work as price continues to charge on. Its worth your time looking at every FL on the LTF and asking yourself where the true limit of the FL is and hence what price level needs to be breached to constitute an engulf. As we are basing our understanding of what price is doing on the engulf of a price level, this is something worth pondering. Here is an example. We expect that the inner boundary of the zone to be the price where remaining stacks of orders are waiting for execution. Since all we have is the chart, we can spot it by a closer look at the candles. There we look where was the last trade before one side overcome the other. Thinking in Order flow terminology, we may suspect that if one side overcome the other, there might be more orders of the winner side which couldent be filled due to less orders of the loosing side. IF : One thing which I have mentioned many times before, but not yet in Markepedia (soon to be remedied), is that in a bigger picture range, Supply and Demand zones near the edges may not hold as well as others. Fakeout often occur, because price is attracted to the limits of the range. Benhur : Nothing promises that zone will hold price, even at rst visit. The zones we mark on the charts are mainly a mapping of decisions in the market. Decision can take price either way. Zones are meant to be broken, and this market decision has its own signi cance too. As further you go with your reading skills, you will be able read the hints and clues for zones to hold or to break. Your task at this time, is to train your eyes de ning the zones.Your next step, is to investigate how price is behaving around these zones. There are few things you should bare in mind while you do this work: 1. Be aware of how price had printed the zone you marked, what it was reacting to, and how the decision of price to move further look like. 2. Be aware of how price is approaching the Zones, what is the dynamic. 3. Is price come from a valid opposite zone? Remember that price goes from Demand to Supply and vice versa. https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/homework-dbr-and-rbd/27-drop-base-rallies-and-rally-base-drops?start=1000 35/42 7/27/2018 Drop Base Rallies and Rally Base Drops - Page 41 - RTM Community 4. Be aware of the reaction of the rst touch, how deep it went inside, what had HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT stopped it if any? 5. What are higher or lower TF tell you. SD discipline is a Multi time frame concept. We trade price levels, not candles, so Story may vary on di erent TF. 6. (More Advanced) Look for correlations with Index and other pairs. It might look intimidating, but actually it's should be very simple. Zones are always a reaction of past Price Action (aka: always look left). As much as you can go back in history, the better you understand be of how price move. There is no randomness for this market, all can be explained with PA reaction, result, decision. When you're doing the DBR/RBD homework, keep that in mind and drag your zones to the right to see how price interacts with them in the future. That will really reinforce the Supply to Demand/Demand to Supply concept and will help when looking at others like FL, FTR, and QM. Posts: 218 Thank you received: 253 Hey Mohsin, Here's what I see on the chart. I have noted a little RBD and DBR within the down trend. I would consider these of lesser importance but if you extend them to the right you can see price reacting off of them as well. I've included them to show you that sometimes we get a longer base in our DBR/RBD. The two of note currently are the top and bottom ones limiting the current flag. I would put the base as the bottom of the candle on this one (the giant pin bar) as the next bar breaks away from it. That pin candle indicates a movement up then down which can also conceal a flag in the LTFs. On this TF I would consider it the base for simplicity's sake. You can get crazy with drawing every blip on the chart and end up with something that will confuse the hell out of you :). Page 49 - RTM Community HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT My homework with explanations at each point A) First DBR B) First RBD (There is a reaction that brings price back to the first demand zone, price flags after touching demand creating a small demand zone on top) Prices reaction to this demand zone cuts through supply at B and this becomes demand C) RBD with a FTB bringing price back to the flag made on top of demand zone at A D) Price reacts to this demand moves away before a FTB pinbar - price easily cuts through supply at C E) RBD - followed by compression down to flip zone from supply at C - from here there is a strong bull move in price that easily breaks supply at E and this becomes demand F) Price is capped and following the indecision there is a RBD formed G) FTB to the strong level created after compression from E H) Price moves up to H where its the FTB to new FTR (plays within this PAZ) I) Bulls are now in control and price is easily able to move down to the price cap at the bottom with a small speed bump from demand at D G) New supply formed where there was previously supply to the left Thanks in advance for all the help! https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/homework-dbr-and-rbd/27-drop-base-rallies-and-rally-base-drops?start=1200 16/34 7/27/2018 Drop Base Rallies and Rally Base Drops - A: Don't get too hung up on the candle count. Focus more on how the price moved away from the level. You want to see a violent burst of liquidity (pole) coming out of the level. What defines a base it that price moves up or down, bases (consolidates, congests, clusters, ect) then moves again either up or down. https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/homework-dbr-and-rbd/27-drop-base-rallies-and-rally-base-drops?start=100 9/34 7/27/2018 Drop Base Rallies and Rally Base Drops - Page 5 - RTM Community Here are the variations. The standard DBD and RBR then the RBR and DBD then RBD HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT during downtrend and DBR during uptrend. Hopefully this could give you a better understanding. However as you have alluded to, H/L or S/R levels are almost always an intrinsic part to the development of any base. If you can find the levels responsible for the bases it can give you a much holistic picture on the chart. Page 50 - RTM Community Thank you received: 56 HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT pin bar is more like this Characteristics of the Pin Bar Formation � The pin bar should have a long upper or lower tail...the tail is also sometimes called the "wick" or the "shadow"...they all mean the same thing. It's the "pointy" part of the pin bar that literally looks like a "tail" and that shows rejection or false break of a level. � The area between the open and close of the pin bar is called the "body" or "real body". It is typically colored white or another light color when the close was higher than the open and black or another dark color when the close was lower than the open. � The open and close of the pin bar should be very close together or equal (same price), the closer the better. � The open and close of the pin bar are near one end of the bar, the closer to the end the better. � The shadow or tail of the pin bar sticks out (protrudes) from the surrounding 22/31 https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/homework-dbr-and-rbd/27-drop-base-rallies-and-rally-base-drops?start=1225 7/27/2018 Drop Base Rallies and Rally Base Drops - Page 50 - RTM Community price bars, the longer the tail of the pin bar the better. We really don't trade those levels directly because this is what classic supply and demand traders do and as we know plain SD trading is just gambling with an (small) edge (IF). The purpose of this homework is to get a feel for basic market structure and to train your eye... And watch out for some tricks too (what happens on ignored levels on return and what happens on stacked levels). Price moves from supply to demand and vice versa. Once you study flag limits you will understand the relationship betweenthe RBD/DBR and FL concept ps. to your question, it makes sense to mark all RBDs and DBRs strong or weak as long as the basic structure is present. First of all, this is a wonderful experience for me to be with you here and learn all this awesome stuff. Next is my HW about caps on price. I used random charts and random segments of them - different TFs. It is really important for me (and my trading) to be as consistent as possible, so here are my rules how I marked rectangles. According to my understanding (mostly coming from the IFs video about the caps) I marked the most important ones, which I identified by liquidity gaps in them. First edge is of course high/low of the cap, but the second edge is open of the last green candle before drop in RBDs and open of the last red candle before the rally in DBR - that is according to my observations the most precise place, where the decision was made to turn the price (IMHO). (If there is no prior candle of different color befor price goes away i marked whole candle in base of the move). note: it really depends on how the rectangle is placed. Sometimes price bounce from the very edges of the base, sometimes from the edge of liquidity gap, but mostly, when I don't want rectangles to be too big, rule above can be applied. note2 : red rectangles don't have reaction if I consider both edges of the rectangle. Price react to them though, but not precisely. note3 : it is obvious that RBD/DBR that are reactions to previous caps are much less important to future visits of price (and it was confirmed by IF and others all over the place ), however price tends to bounce from them too. note4 : because I really like statistics, here are the results from 87 reactions to caps - just for fun, of course: 67 was ok for scalp at least, 4 was fine to trade after they break and 16 was bad.
